findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the dish machine (heat function is not working, PIC is aware and not utilizing it) to be pulling 10-50 ppm of chlorine bleach. Facility is utilizing only the bleach component for sanitizing purposes. Kohl’s will be called by PIC to service the dish machine. Multiple runs were conducted and each produced either 10-50 ppm or 0 ppm with test strips. Facility has test strips to check concentration level. Facility also has a maximum registering thermometer to check heat sanitization levels with the heat function is properly working. Inspector will follow-up on 1/17/23. This is a 3 day follow-up; however, the Inspector has prior SCDPH engagements (conference) and county issued holiday on Monday, 1/16/23. Inspector instructed facility to utilize the 3 compartment sink - wash, rinse, sanitize. Dish machine may be used to wash and rinse, sanitize must occur in the 3 compartment sink with correct bleach concentration (50-200 ppm).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-202.12: (A) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be used according to LAW(C), Manufacturer’s directions (indicate for use in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT) (P), conditions of certification (if applicable) (P), and additional conditions (if applicable) (C).

The bottle of bleach used to make sani buckets in the facility does not have direction for making a solution intended for food contact surfaces.  Directions observed seem to indicate uses for laundry and bathroom use. Inspector discussed with the PIC. PIC found instructions on the internet for the making a solution intended for food contact surfaces and printed them out during the inspection to correct. Inspector reviewed label requirements with the PIC  emphasizing EPA registrations numbers and instructions for making solutions intended for sanitizing food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices. 

Inspector could not get a temperature reading in the hot water sanitizing dish machine higher than 151 degrees Fahrenheit. Multiple attempts were made using both the inspector's thermometer and the facility's (both registered within 1 degree of each other). Follow up will be set for 2/15/21. Until the machine can be verified as sanitizing effectively, the facility will use a Chlorine solution to sanitize after washing in the dish machine.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.112  (Pf) The inspector's maximum registering thermometer registered 151°-158°F in the dish machine over several attempts. The critical limit for temperature based sanitizing is 160°F. Maintenance was contacted during the inspection. The follow up is set for February 10, 2020.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.112 (A) The temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 194F, or less than 180F.
The dish machine was only registering approximately 160F at the manifold and was not registering at safe sanitizing temperatures on the inspector's maximum registering test strip. Maintenance was called and began work on the machine during the inspection. A follow up is set for 10 business days (5/9/19). The machine was switched to chemical sanitizing during the inspection to continue operation.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

Observed a bowl stored in a container of Oreo cookie pieces. Discussed the use of a scoop with a handle with the PIC. Stated that ready to eat foods should be handled and distributed in a manner so as to prevent contamination by the hands. The bowl (being use as a scoop) as well as the contents of the container was discarded during the inspection.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

Observed 2 can openers to have blades soiled from use. Discussed with the person in charge and directed to clean after heavy use. Can openers were cleaned during the inspection.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

Observed a gatorade that had been drunk from to be stored in the walk in cooler with foods intended for consumption by consumers. Discussed with the manager and directed for the drink to be moved to the shelf designated for employee foods.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment: 750-820(a) Observed a food employee wash and rinse a blender in the two part sink in the salad prep area. All food contact surfaces shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use. When manual ware washing, a sink with no fewer than three compartments shall be used to properly wash, rinse, and sanitize equipment and utensils. Facility has a three compartment sink and a dish washing machine. Food employees should utilize the three compartment sink and dish washing machine to properly wash, rinse, and sanitize food contact surfaces. Blender was taken to the dish machine to be properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Facility should ensure that all food employees responsible for ware washing are knowledgeable on proper wash, rinse, and sanitize procedures including but not limited to appropriate sanitizer concentrations, contact time, and how to prevent potential contamination of clean, sanitized food equipment.

findings.title: Sanitizing temperature
findings.comment: 750-830 Upon entering the facility the manager indicated the dish machine was activing fickle. The machine was allowed to run through a cycle at least a dozen times and never truly indicated a temperature over 160F on the thermometer. Maximum registering thermometers from the facility and inspector were ran through a cycle and the maximum temperature indicated was only 155F  - confirmed on both thermometers. The facility is going to use the machine to wash and rinse trays and then wipe the trays with a wiping cloth solution of 100ppm Cl. All other equipment will be washed and rinse through the machine and allowed to rest in a sanitizing solutionn of 50ppm Cl for 60 seconds.   All hot water for sanitizing dishes and equipment must be a minimum of 180F when it leaves the dishwashing machine manifold in order to kill pathogens.  Properly sanitize all items. Check and maintain the dishwasher frequently.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the ice flap to the ice machine to be soiled with a small amount of mold accumulation. 2) Observed the coffee spout in the self serve area to be soiled. Clean the food contact surfaces. Both food contact surfaces were corrected during the inspection.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed a small amount of rodent droppings in the dry storage area. The floor was cleaned during the inspection.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed a sanitizer bucket to have no bleach.  Bleach was added during the inspection to correct the violation.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.
